comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated `manager.update(running)` in `resumeChild`**

This PR adds an identical status update directly above the pre-existing one
(`task_executor.dart:379-389`):

```dart
      await manager.update(
        id,
        status: SubagentStatus.running,
        clearError: true,
      );
      await manager.update(          // <-- pre-existing (context line)
        id,
        status: SubagentStatus.running,
        clearError: true,
      );
```

`SubagentManager.update` re-stamps `lastActivity` (`subagent_manager.dart:416`)
and calls `_persist(force: true)` (`subagent_manager.dart:421`), so every
resume now emits a duplicate `SubagentEvent` to the events stream and appends
TWO distinct registry snapshots (different `lastActivity` timestamps — the
snapshot deduper cannot suppress them) to the session ledger. Functionally
idempotent, but it is accidental duplication introduced by this change and
doubles a durability-critical append on every resume.

Fix: delete the added block (keep a single `update` call). If the intent was
to set `running` before `carryPendingReply`, move the single call above the
carry block instead of adding a second one.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: clear-before-persist ordering can permanently lose an acked reply**

`resumeChild` runs:

```dart
pendingReply = manager.carryPendingReply(id);   // clears handle.lastReply + _persist()
if (pendingReply != null) {
  _capture?.persistCarriedReply(id, pendingReply);  // throws through on redaction failure
}
```

but `carryPendingReply` (`subagent_manager.dart:808`) clears `handle.lastReply`
and persists the CLEARED snapshot BEFORE `persistCarriedReply` runs. If
`persistCarriedReply` throws — `_redactOrThrow` invokes the host-supplied
redactor (`deliverables.dart:252`), an arbitrary host pipeline that can throw —
then in that moment:

1. the handle's `lastReply` is already null,
2. the durable registry snapshot already persisted the cleared state,
3. no artifact was written.

The resume fails with the named error (good), but the reply is now
unrecoverable: a retry `task_resume` finds `lastReply == null &&
duplicateReplies == 0`, so `carryPendingReply` returns null and the reply that
was acked "delivered" is silently gone. That contradicts the documented E5
intent in `persistCarriedReply` ("the resume fails with a NAMED error rather
than losing the reply silently") and this PR's own core guarantee for the
exact kill→resume path it introduces.

Fix (either):
- Persist the carried artifact from the snapshot BEFORE clearing: split
  `carryPendingReply` into peek + clear, and only clear after
  `persistCarriedReply` succeeds; or
- Wrap `_capture?.persistCarriedReply(...)` so a throw restores
  `handle.lastReply` (and `duplicateReplies`) and re-persists before
  propagating.

Note the same window exists between `carryPendingReply`'s `_persist()` of the
cleared state and the artifact `store.put` — restoring-on-throw covers both.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: blocking render can emit two contradictory pointer lines**

In `_renderResultBody`, the over-preview branch writes its own pointer line:

```dart
buffer
  ..writeln(output.substring(0, outputPreviewChars))
  ..writeln('…')
  ..write('[Full output: agent://${result.id}]');   // line 175
pointerTailed = true;
```

`pointerTailed` is only consumed when `leadWithPointer` is true (the async
envelope). The blocking renderer (`_renderResult`, line ~843) calls this helper
with the default `leadWithPointer: false` and then UNCONDITIONALLY appends its
own tail:

```dart
'\n[${result.truncated ? 'Truncated output' : 'Full output'}: agent://${result.id}]'
```

When the stored output is both over the 5000-char preview AND truncated
(`truncated: true` — >5000 lines or ~500 KB, see `_capOutput`), the parent
sees:

```
…[truncated]
[Full output: agent://id]
[Truncated output: agent://id]
```

— two pointer lines for the same id with contradictory labels. Cosmetic, but
model-facing text: drop the body-side pointer line when `leadWithPointer` is
false (the caller always adds the tail), or let the helper own the tail
entirely.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the `[explicit reply]` body is unvalidated child text inside a structured envelope**

The new parent-visible render interpolates the reply body raw between the
`[explicit reply]` / `[explicit reply end]` markers (line 159):

```dart
buffer
  ..writeln('[explicit reply]')
  ..write(reply)
  ..write('\n[explicit reply end]');
```

Nothing escapes or fences the body, so a child (model-written text) can embed
the literal line `[explicit reply end]` early and follow it with forged
structural lines — e.g. `[deliverable complete: agent://kid2 …]` verdicts for a
sibling, or another `[explicit reply]` block. This is the same
synthetic-line-injection class the codebase already defends against elsewhere
(`DeliverableCapture._cleanReportId` strips `[\r\n\[\]]` from child-chosen ids
"so a hostile-looking id cannot inject synthetic lines — review hygiene, issue
#1829"). The reply body rides a same-trust channel (the child's final message
is equally raw), so this is not a new trust boundary — but this render is now
the PRIMARY deliverable surface for the parent model, and anything that
machine-parses the envelope (or the parent model skimming it) can be misled.

Options: fence the body (```` ``` ````), indent it, or sanitize the known
marker sequences (`[explicit reply end]`, `[deliverable ` at line start) the
same way ids are sanitized. At minimum, document in `_renderResultBody`'s doc
comment that the body is untrusted and markers are best-effort.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `addTearDown(() => sub.cancel)` never cancels the subscription**

In the "carried reply + fresh reply combine" test (AC6):

```dart
final sub = wiring.jobs.completions.listen(notices.add);
addTearDown(() => sub.cancel);   // line 753 — returns the tear-off, never calls it
```

The arrow function evaluates `sub.cancel` (a method tear-off) and discards it —
the subscription is never cancelled. Every other test in this file uses the
invoking form `addTearDown(() => sub.cancel())` (lines 609, 643, 666, 695,
725). Harmless today because `wiring.dispose()` closes the broadcast
controller, but it is a latent leak if the test grows teardowns that depend on
cancellation order. Change to `addTearDown(() => sub.cancel());`.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Thread 2 — `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6xeUJH` (task_executor.dart:377) — clear-before-persist can lose an acked reply

**Fixed** with the reviewer's first option: `carryPendingReply` is split into
peek + clear, and the handle clears only after the carried artifact is durable.

- `lib/src/task/subagent_manager.dart` — `carryPendingReply` is replaced by
  `peekPendingReply(id)` (snapshot without mutating the handle) and
  `clearPendingReply(id)` (clears `lastReply`/`duplicateReplies`, emits,
  persists); `carryPendingReply`'s only caller was `resumeChild`.
- `lib/src/task/task_executor.dart` — the resume start now runs
  `peekPendingReply` → `_capture?.persistCarriedReply(...)` → `clearPendingReply`.
  If `persistCarriedReply` throws (host redactor / `store.put` — the whole
  window the reviewer pointed out), the resume still fails with the named
  error, but the reply is **still on the handle** and still durable: a retry
  `task_resume` finds it again and carries it (at-least-once; never a silent
  loss — matches the documented E5 intent).

Regression test ("a redactor failure while persisting the carried reply leaves
the acked reply intact for the retry resume"): a redactor that throws at carry
time fails resume 1; under the old order `lastReply` was already `null` (the
test failed with `Actual: null`); the test then retries over the SAME manager
with a healthy redactor and asserts the completion surfaces
`THE-PENDING-REPORT` verbatim plus a resolvable `agent://` artifact.

# Thread 3 — `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6xeULn` (task_tool.dart:175) — contradictory pointer lines

**Fixed** with the reviewer's first option: the helper's body-side pointer
line is now written **only when `leadWithPointer` is true** (the async
envelope, which owns its pointer). The blocking renderer
(`leadWithPointer: false`) appends its truncation-aware tail as before, so the
over-preview-and-truncated case renders exactly one pointer line:

```

[Truncated output: agent://id]
```

  longer writes `[Full output: agent://…]` for the blocking renderer.
- Tests ("blocking render: over-preview AND truncated output carries exactly
  one pointer line" — a 5001-line child output exercises `truncated: true` +
  over-preview: asserts no `[Full output: agent://Kid]`, exactly one
  `agent://Kid]` occurrence; "async envelope keeps its single over-preview
  pointer (guard)" — 450-char output > the 400-char envelope preview keeps
  exactly one pointer, pinning the async path while the blocking path is
  fixed).

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Thread 4 — `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6xeUOQ` (task_tool.dart:159) — unvalidated reply body in the envelope

**Fixed** with the sanitize option (the reviewer's middle ground, same class
as the #1829 id sanitizer), plus the requested documentation:

- `lib/src/task/task_tool.dart` — `_defuseEnvelopeMarkers(reply)` runs on the
  reply body before it is interpolated into the `[explicit reply]` block.
  Line-leading (whitespace-tolerant) envelope markers are defused by stripping
  the structural brackets — the exact mechanism `_cleanReportId` uses for
  child-chosen ids:
  - `[explicit reply]` / `[explicit reply end]` — the body cannot close the
    block early or open a nested block,
  - `[deliverable ` / `[deliverable:` — no forged sibling verdict lines,
  - `[completed_without_reply` — the gap notice cannot be forged,
  - `[Full output:` / `[Truncated output:` — no impostor output pointers.
  Text content is preserved (defusing is not dropping), and the doc comment on
  `_renderResultBody` now documents that the body is untrusted child text and
  the markers are best-effort.
- Test ("line-leading forged envelope markers inside the reply body are
  defused"): a body carrying `[explicit reply end]`, a forged
  `[deliverable complete: agent://Rival …]` verdict, a second `[explicit
  reply]`, an impostor `[Full output: agent://Impostor]`, and an indented
  end-marker renders with exactly ONE real terminator, zero line-leading
  forged structural lines, one real block opener, and the body content intact.
  Under the old render the test found 3 `[explicit reply end]` occurrences.

comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: The gh-1951 deliverable guarantee is correctly implemented and well tested: 19 AC/edge tests pass (`dart test test/task/reply_delivery_guarantee_test.dart`), the touched suites pass, `dart analyze` is clean, and the honest-ack / resumed-completion design matches the ticket ACs. Two important issues and three suggestions remain — none block the merge.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `task_executor.dart:379` — duplicated `manager.update(running)` in `resumeChild` (double event + double forced registry append per resume)
- ⚠️ `task_executor.dart:375` — `carryPendingReply` clears + persists the cleared handle BEFORE `persistCarriedReply`; a throwing host redactor at resume start permanently loses the acked reply (contradicts the documented E5 "never lose the reply")
- 💡 `task_tool.dart:175` — blocking render can emit two contradictory pointer lines (`[Full output: …]` + `[Truncated output: …]`) when output is both over-preview and truncated
- 💡 `task_tool.dart:159` — `[explicit reply]` body is unvalidated child text that can contain the literal end marker or forge `[deliverable …]` verdict lines (same synthetic-line class issue #1829 sanitized ids for)
- 💡 `reply_delivery_guarantee_test.dart:753` — `addTearDown(() => sub.cancel)` never invokes `cancel`

**Next Steps**:
1. Delete the duplicated `manager.update` block at `task_executor.dart:379-383` (keep one)
2. Reorder: persist the carried artifact from the snapshot BEFORE `carryPendingReply` clears the handle (or restore + re-persist on throw)
3. Drop the body-side pointer line when `leadWithPointer` is false, or align its label with the truncation state
4. Optional: escape/fence the reply body or document the untrusted-body caveat
5. Optional test nit: `addTearDown(() => sub.cancel())` at line 753
